question: I have been given a council parking ticket. How long do I have to challenge it, and what happens if my challenge is rejected?
answer: You have 28 days to challenge a penalty charge notice (PCN), and if you do so within 14 days and your challenge is rejected, you may only have to pay 50% of the fine. If your informal challenge is rejected, you will receive a 'notice to owner' explaining how to pay or make a formal challenge, which you then have 28 days to submit. If your formal challenge is rejected, you will get a 'notice of rejection' that gives you 28 days to pay or appeal to an independent tribunal. If you do not pay or appeal following that rejection, you will have to pay a late penalty ('charge certificate').

question: I am being made redundant after six years in my job. How much notice am I entitled to, how is my notice pay worked out, and could my employer pay me instead of letting me work it?
answer: Having been employed for six years, your statutory redundancy notice period is one week’s notice for each year, though you should check your contract as your employer can give you more than this minimum, but cannot give you less. Your notice pay is based on the average you earned per week over the 12 weeks before your notice period starts, or what you would have earned normally if you were paid less than usual because you were on furlough due to coronavirus. Your employer can end your employment without notice and pay you instead of giving you a notice period provided that your contract includes ‘payment in lieu of notice’. Under payment in lieu of notice, you get all the basic pay you would have received during the notice period, and you may get extras such as pension contributions or private health care insurance if they are in your contract.

question: I rent my flat in Cardiff. Does my landlord have to protect my deposit, and by when?
answer: Your landlord must put your deposit in a government-approved tenancy deposit scheme if you rent your home on an assured periodic tenancy (APT). If you do not rent your home on an APT, your landlord can accept valuable items instead of money, and these will not be covered by a scheme. Where protection applies, your landlord or letting agent must put your deposit in the scheme within 30 days of getting it. In England and Wales, your deposit can be registered with the Deposit Protection Service, MyDeposits (including deposits that were held by Capita), or the Tenancy Deposit Scheme.
